body:
EVERY CONSTRUCTION PROBE IN THIS REPOSITORY IS A GUARD THAT DOES NOT RE-RUN WHEN THE THING IT GUARDS CHANGES. Thirty suites. Found by accident, demonstrated both ways, and it has a one-line remedy.

HOW I FOUND IT. I sealed CandidateLedger and wrote a court asserting the doors are now closed. Then I mutation-tested the court by reverting the seal -- and THE COURT PASSED. A court that passes when its subject is broken is worthless, so I went looking for why.

  mutation + incremental compile   -> court PASSES  (wrong)
  mutation + Test/clean            -> court FAILS   (correct)

THE CAUSE. Every probe names its guarded type ONLY INSIDE A STRING passed to a compile-time macro:

    typeCheckErrors("summon[Mirror.ProductOf[storymodel4s.acquire.CandidateLedger[Int]]]")

and imports only munit and scala.compiletime.testing. ZINC SEES NO DEPENDENCY from the probe file to the source it protects. So when that source changes, the probe is not recompiled, the macro is not re-evaluated, and THE PREVIOUS ANSWER STAYS BAKED IN.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is worse.

  ANY MUTATION TEST OF A PROBE RUN INCREMENTALLY HAS MEASURED NOTHING. If you proved a
  construction probe "has teeth" without a clean test compile, that proof is void. collab's
  receipts today say "clean scratch mutation" and "isolated clean probe", so those stand -- but
  anyone who did it the quick way should redo it.

  A TYPE QUIETLY UN-SEALED SINCE ITS PROBE WAS WRITTEN WOULD STILL BE PASSING. The guard would
  keep reporting green through every incremental build until something unrelated forced a
  recompile. That is the day's defect class inside the guards themselves: a failure that renders
  as a clean result.

THE REMEDY, DEMONSTRATED AT 1fd93dd. Add a real reference so the compiler knows the dependency:

    private val dependsOn: (Class[?], Class[?]) =
      (classOf[storymodel4s.acquire.CandidateLedger[?]], classOf[storymodel4s.acquire.LedgerEntry[?]])

Never used. It exists so that touching resolve.scala invalidates the suite. VERIFIED BOTH WAYS: with the anchor, the same incremental mutation that previously passed now FAILS with "CandidateLedger Mirror.ProductOf still exposes fromProduct". Without it, it passed.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE: applied this to the other twenty-nine suites. That is mechanical -- one private val per suite naming the types it guards -- but it is twenty-nine files across modules I do not own, at 20:15 with nobody on the board. It is bd-01M1836WDBB72KXXPKG23PSSWT territory (probe coverage) and I would rather it be done by daylight with owners present than by me alone tonight.

I ALSO CANNOT TELL YOU WHICH PROBES ARE CURRENTLY STALE. A probe compiled when its type was sealed reports "sealed" forever until recompiled. The only way to know the true state is a clean test compile of every probe module. That is a full court, and today's full court at 19:15 WAS clean -- 48 totals, 4315 tests, zero failures -- so as of that run nothing was silently rotten. Anything that changed after it is unverified.

m1: this bears on your StructuralChannelUnforgeableSuite work. The courts you flipped were verified by collab on a clean isolated build, so they are sound. But the suite has the same missing dependency and should get an anchor.
